blocks.content: Any person who does not receive a decision within the time specified or is aggrieved by a decision of the CPIO may prefer a First Appeal under Section 19(1) of the RTI Act.

rows: First Appellate Authority (Senior Officer in same Department)
Central or State Information Commission (CIC / SIC)
Within 30 days from decision or expiry of 30-day CPIO limit
Within 90 days from FAA decision date or expiry period
30 days (extendable up to 45 days for special reasons)
No specific time limit prescribed under the Act
Can impose penalty up to ₹25,000 on CPIO under Sec 20(1)

items: Section 19(1) governs First Appeal, whereas Section 19(3) governs Second Appeal in the RTI Act, 2005.
While First Appeal has a statutory disposal limit of 30-45 days, the RTI Act specifies no fixed time frame for CIC/SIC to dispose of a Second Appeal.
Penalties up to ₹25,000 under Section 20(1) can only be imposed by the Information Commission during a Second Appeal or Complaint, not by the First Appellate Authority.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: A First Appeal is filed before an officer senior in rank to the CPIO within the same public authority under Section 19(1).
The First Appellate Authority (FAA) must decide the appeal within 30 days, extendable up to 45 days with written justification.
A Second Appeal lies with the Central Information Commission (CIC) or State Information Commission (SIC) under Section 19(3).
Second Appeals must be preferred within 90 days from the date on which the FAA decision was received or ought to have been rendered.
The onus to prove that a denial of request was justified lies entirely on the Public Information Officer (CPIO/SPIO).
